# pbs_apt_standard_repository (Resource)

Adds one of the standard APT repositories of Proxmox Backup Server to a node: `enterprise`, `no-subscription` or `test`. The counterpart of `proxmox_apt_standard_repository` in bpg/proxmox.

Creating the resource has PBS add the repository's entry, enabled — on PBS 4, to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources` for `enterprise` and to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/proxmox.sources` for the others. When the node has an entry of the repository already, PBS enables it instead, and leaves it as it is when it is enabled — but for the test repository's component as PBS 3 wrote it, `pbstest`, which PBS 4.2.1 and later rewrite to `pbs-test`. `file_path` and `index` tell where the entry is, for a `pbs_apt_repository` that enables or disables it later; this resource does not change it again while it is there. A refresh that finds no entry of the repository removes it from the state, and the next apply adds the entry again.

PBS cannot remove an entry, so **destroying the resource disables the repository**: every enabled entry of it, which is what PBS's own interface offers. bpg/proxmox leaves the repository enabled instead; here destroy undoes what create did as far as PBS allows, so that, for instance, changing `handle` from `test` to `no-subscription` replaces the one by the other rather than leaving both enabled. To stop managing a repository and keep it enabled, remove the resource from the state (`terraform state rm`, or a `removed` block with `destroy = false`) instead of destroying it.

~> **One resource per repository.** Destroying a resource disables its repository even when another resource has it too, and that one then reads it disabled without planning a change. So manage a repository with one resource only, on one spelling of the node; move a resource to another address — renaming it, changing its `count` or `for_each` key — with a `moved` block rather than by destroying and creating it; and do not combine `create_before_destroy` with a replacement. An entry that lists the components of two standard repositories is disabled as an entry of either.

Reading the source files needs `Sys.Audit on /`, changing them `Sys.Modify on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The no-subscription repository, for a host without a subscription. PBS
# adds its entry to /etc/apt/sources.list.d/proxmox.sources, or enables the
# entry the host has.
resource "pbs_apt_standard_repository" "no_subscription" {
  handle = "no-subscription"
}

# The test repository, kept off until it is needed. PBS adds its entry
# enabled; the pbs_apt_repository, which refers to where the standard
# repository says the entry is, disables it right after, in the same apply.
resource "pbs_apt_standard_repository" "test" {
  handle = "test"
}

resource "pbs_apt_repository" "test" {
  file_path = pbs_apt_standard_repository.test.file_path
  index     = pbs_apt_standard_repository.test.index
  enabled   = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `handle` (String) Standard repository to add: `enterprise`, the stable repository for hosts with a subscription, `no-subscription`, for hosts without one, or `test`, for testing new releases. Changing it replaces the resource, which disables the old repository.

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node whose APT source files to manage: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. PBS is a single node, so both name the same files: do not manage one entry or repository under both. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Description of the repository as PBS shows it.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether an enabled entry of the repository is there; false when its entries are disabled, such as by a `pbs_apt_repository`.
- `file_path` (String) Path of the file that holds the repository's entry — the first one, should there be several. Null when the provider cannot tell which entry PBS counts: PBS 4.2.1 and later also count an entry with another URI, such as a local mirror or the download server over `https://`, by the key that signs it.
- `id` (String) `<node>,<handle>`, such as `localhost,no-subscription`.
- `index` (Number) Index of that entry in the file, from 0; null when `file_path` is.
- `name` (String) Name of the repository as PBS shows it, such as `No-Subscription`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_apt_standard_repository.no_subscription
  identity = {
    node   = "localhost"
    handle = "no-subscription"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `handle` (String) Handle of the standard repository, such as `no-subscription`.
- `node` (String) Node name, such as `localhost`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_apt_standard_repository.no_subscription
  id = "localhost,no-subscription"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A standard repository the node has is imported by <node>,<handle>, as in
# bpg/proxmox: the node is localhost or the node's host name, the handle
# enterprise, no-subscription or test.
terraform import pbs_apt_standard_repository.no_subscription localhost,no-subscription
```
